statement_en: Across museum flying-fish specimens, pectoral fin length scales with standard length as SL^b with the exponent inside its 95% CI [1.017, 1.099] (OLS on log-log, n = 49, b = 1.058, r^2 = 0.983).
missing_inputs: Narrow scope to the 3 sampled species, named, with life_stages covering larva/juvenile/adult as pooled, ranges SL 1.68-24 cm, and state 'preserved specimens, pooled across species and ontogeny'. Do not declare Exocoetidae.

State in statement_en and evidence.caveats that this is a record bound: the CI of a pooled OLS slope in a single sample of 49 specimens, with no held-back data and about 3 independent species-level observations. It is not an impossibility.

Fix the provenance: reconcile the cited sha256 (9c941299f5869e56) with the repo file (4f654c701f6196dc), then recompute the OLS slope and CI from the correctly hashed Data S1A. Declare 1.017 and 1.099 as derived with the stated derivation (the recomputation script and its rounding), not found by string match.  [WITHDRAWN: the cited hash is correct; the hash check itself was the bug - see corrections]

Make C6 evaluable: add a finLengthExponent to wildtype.json for in-scope organisms. Compute it only from within-species size series where such data exist (for example, per-species slopes from the same Data S1A rows), or else keep the law out of the Studio.
Consider reporting the exponent per species, or an RMA slope, so that the pooled Simpson-type artefact the proponent flags can be checked.
would_constrain_if_supplied: Once the listed inputs are declared, this statement binds designs through disc-pectoral-length-allometry and can be reproposed. Until then it is sound and unevaluable, which is why it is recorded here rather than as a failure.

C1_binds_something_real.reason: a witness satisfies the law, and the in-range design {"finLengthExponent":0} is rejected by 1.017 ≤ q.finLengthExponent

C2_constants_sourced.reason: all 2 non-structural constant(s) declared with an allowed kind and a source; every constant was found in its cited source by a GET

C3_scope_honest.reason: Scope declares the whole family Exocoetidae with empty life_stages and empty ranges. The evidence is 49 preserved specimens from 3 species, pooled across species and ontogeny, SL 1.68-24 cm, larvae and juveniles included. The proponent concedes the scope is wider than the evidence, and the critic agrees. The family has roughly 70 species, and the 3 sampled species are not even named in the candidate.

C4_independent.reason: E5 bounds the pectoral/SL ratio at a single size, and this law bounds the log-log slope across sizes. A design with every specimen's ratio inside [0.406, 0.823] can still have a slope of 0.8 or 1.25, which E5 permits and this law rejects. E1 and E2 constrain mass and area exponents and share no quantity with it. It is not a definition. It is a partly related summary of the same Daane Data S1 file as E5, so it is weak as independent evidence, but it does add a constraint E5 does not impose.

C5_consistent.reason: propose.mjs constructed a joint witness with every accepted law whose scope overlaps

C6_wild_type_survives.reason: 24 wild-type organism(s) are in scope but none carries finLengthExponent: the law cannot be evaluated against a real animal, so it may not be promoted

C7_not_circular.reason: The proponent concedes this is a record bound: the 95% CI of a pooled OLS fit, tested on the same 49 specimens (which clustered by species/lot give about 3 independent species-level observations), with nothing held back. The witness is the fitted point estimate, so it passes by construction. The statement is not sold as an impossibility, so this is not an un-fixable REJECT. But neither statement_en nor evidence.caveats labels it as a record bound, which the criteria require. The critic's 'fatal' rating overreaches for the same reason: the law claims a sample statistic, not a mechanism. The failure is the missing label, which is fixable.

debate.ruling: The law binds a single quantity, the pooled log-log slope of pectoral length on SL, to the 95% CI [1.017, 1.099] from 49 preserved specimens of 3 species. It does add a size-scaling constraint that E5's single-size ratio band does not. It cannot be promoted for three reasons. C6 is unclear because no in-scope wild-type organism carries the exponent. C3 fails because the family-wide scope rests on 3 unnamed species with pooled ontogeny. C7 fails because a record bound is not labelled as one. The C2 gate passes, but the evidence checker shows the 'found' verdicts were matcher false positives, the cited file hash does not match, and the CI bounds were never recomputed. None of the defects is un-fixable, so this is NEEDS-WORK, not REJECT.
debate.debate_limitations: PROVENANCE BOUND on this ruling: in the round that produced it, the debate's critic and evidence-checker workers made ZERO web tool calls despite having them (recorded in pipeline/leanbio/debate/DEBATE-RESULTS.md). So no counterexample in this round came from the literature: every rejection was caught by a mechanical check against data already in the repository. The "debated" label therefore means "survived the repo's own gates", not "survived a literature search for counterexamples".

scope_note: Static mirror of lean/registry/open-questions/. An OPEN QUESTION is a question this project holds unsettled, with an arm per live position, each arm's evidence quoted from its primary source, and a belief `proportion` COMPUTED by pipeline/leanbio/belief.mjs rather than asserted. A proportion orders the arms; it is NOT a probability that an arm is true, and belief-params.json says plainly that its parameters are hand-set and not fitted. No arm of an open question is in any law set, and the guard in openq-lib.mjs refuses to accept a law that asserts one. A FAILED THEOREM is a statement this project tried and could not establish, kept with its reason so nobody reproposes it; `what_survives` says what is still true after the failure. READ `attempted`: a failed-theorem record with `attempted: false` was NEVER TRIED (the single Lean build lock was contended, or it was abandoned on cost, or withheld on purpose), so it is not a result about the statement at all and its `proof_status` says so; the counts report attempted and never-attempted separately for that reason. A NOT-CHECKABLE-IN-PRINCIPLE record is a fourth thing: sound, usually proved, but with no falsifiable direction over any design, so NO input would make it bind -- it carries no `missing_inputs`, because a list of them would read as a to-do and misstate the finding. Arms formalised in Lean are proved internally consistent and are NOT proved true of any organism.
